lucy_customer_ops: FYI a customer in eu-west is seeing a sudden p95 jump to ~600ms after a platform failover 10m ago. They say requests are routing to us-east. Can we triage?
sara_support: Oof. Do we have a trace or sample request id? Any auth errors or 5xx?
lucy_customer_ops: No 5xx, just higher latency. Example request id: r_0a9f3b. Customer attached a trace (sensitive header redacted). They also pasted traceroute showing final hop in us-east.
sara_support: Can someone grab the trace from our trace store + the route metadata (region selected, tier, fallback policy) for r_0a9f3b? Also need the model and variant.
aj_reliability: Pulling trace now. Quick check: our smart-routing logs show a fallback event at 2026-03-17T14:12:03Z for that tenant -> routed to model-variant "llama-13b-q8-dyn@us-east-1" due to dedicated pool exhaustion in eu-west.
mike_network: I ran a quick traceroute from our eu-west ingress (hosted probe) to the customer IP; it went eu-west -> transit-peer -> us-east NAT -> customer. Looks like egress was advertised via the us-east transit for a short window.
sara_support: So two possibilities: 1) smart-routing intentionally fell back to us-east variant, 2) BGP/peering changed and egress left via us-east despite region selection. Which one triggered first?
aj_reliability: Timeline from logs: capacity alarm fired at 14:11:59Z -> routing policy evaluation at 14:12:01Z chose fallback path (allowed by policy) -> request routed at 14:12:03Z. Peering table shows a transient AS path change at 14:11:58Z. Both happened within seconds.
lucy_customer_ops: Customer says they didn't expect cross-region routing on failover—their config pins region to eu-west. They have a dedicated plan but we had an autoscale event.
sara_support: Can you paste their config? Also, did we honor the pin? If they pinned region, fallback should have honored region preference and use queued capacity or return 429, not route cross-region.
aj_reliability: Their app config: `region_preference: eu-west, fallback: allow_cross_region:true` — oh the fallback flag is true. That explains allowed cross-region. But UX mismatch: docs imply pin prevents cross-region unless force. We'll need to update wording.
mike_network: Looking at NAT mapping, egress IP belonged to us-east pool. The transit peer advertised a more specific route for ~30s after a peering flapping event; our routers preferred that path. That made us route egress via us-east even for eu-west-originated containers.
sara_support: Action items: (1) confirm which requests hit cross-region fallback (list of request ids), (2) set temporary override to prevent cross-region fallbacks for this customer, (3) open a network incident for the peering flapping, (4) communicate to customer.
aj_reliability: I'll generate the list: found ~42 requests between 14:12:02Z and 14:12:40Z for tenant X that used us-east variants. Dumping sample trace snippets: ```trace: r_0a9f3b -> route: eu-west-ingress -> us-east-kube-proxy -> model-llama-13b@us-east-1 -> kv-cache hit -> response. latency breakdown: 420ms egress transit + 150ms model infer.```
lucy_customer_ops: Can we repro quickly? Steps? Customer is willing to run tests.
sara_support: Repro steps I recommend: 1) send request with header `X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant>` and `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west` for 1000 short prompts, 2) simulate capacity exhaustion by toggling a capacity limiter in staging or run a high-QPS test to trigger fallback, 3) capture trace and `route.meta` for each request. Example curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -o /tmp/trace.json```
mike_network: For network repro, run a traceroute from our eu-west egress probe during the window and monitor BGP updates: `birdcl -s` and watch for /32 or specific prefix withdrawals/announces.
deploy-bot: config-change user=aj_reliability action=override set tenant=X fallback.allow_cross_region=false expires=2026-03-17T16:00:00Z
sara_support: Thanks. Once override is in place, I want to re-run the high-QPS test to confirm requests are queued or 429'd instead of cross-region routed. We'll notify customer and offer credits for degraded perf.
aj_reliability: Network team confirms a peering flapped due to upstream maintenance; we've flagged the provider and they rolled back. Rolling the override back after 2h once we confirm stability. Also filing docs bug to clarify `region_preference` vs `region_pin` semantics.
lucy_customer_ops: Customer updated: latency back to normal after 15m. They appreciated quick action. Requested the incident notes and whether we can add an account-level lock to disallow cross-region fallback permanently.
sara_support: Noted. I'll create a follow-up ticket: support/12345 to add account-level "disallow_cross_region_fallback" flag and update docs. Closing this thread when ticket created. :white_check_mark:
